The submission was accepted and validated. Here's my account of the work.

## Work performed

I normalized the single supplied seed-0 record (`SKU-0000-10`, marketplace) into a flat identity + attribute observation, exactly per the packet's rules.

**Field derivation:**
| Field | Input | Rule applied | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| brand | `Orion Electronics` | `brand_aliases` display value | `Orion` |
| model | `m2-x` | remove only spaces/hyphens, uppercase | `M2X` |
| pack_size | `"1 pcs"` | parse to integer | `1` |
| capacity | `"1.024 TB"` | decimal TB→GB (×1000) | `capacity_gb: 1024` |
| interface | `"nvme"` | `attribute_aliases` | `NVMe` |
| source / priority | `marketplace` | `source_priority` | `2` |
| entity_id | — | `BRAND_UPPER:MODEL:category:packN` + storage `:gbN` | `ORION:M2X:storage:pack1:gb1024` |

Model and pack_size were both present, so the record resolved (`reason: null`). I intentionally did **not** infer any identity from the title (`Orion M2X new edition`) or attempt conflict resolution, as instructed.

Final artifact value:
```json
{
  "source_sku": "SKU-0000-10",
  "source_row": "C0000-10",
  "source": "marketplace",
  "priority": 2,
  "entity_id": "ORION:M2X:storage:pack1:gb1024",
  "reason": null,
  "brand": "Orion",
  "model": "M2X",
  "category": "storage",
  "pack_size": 1,
  "attributes": {"capacity_gb": 1024, "interface": "NVMe"}
}
```

**Scratch:** logic implemented/verified in `reference_work/normalize.py`; envelope written to `payload.json`.
